text:
sanjay.p: Quick heads-up — starting a short sprint to remove stale admin entitlements and run the periodic access review for Prod KMS keys. Need audit-log queries, rollback playbook, and a canary plan. Who can take KMS/CloudTrail queries? cc @devops_oncall

maria: I can own KMS logs. suggest we pull last 90 days and focus on key admin events + console consoleSignIn by principals with Admin policy.

kevin_h: FYI recert tool flagged ~42 privileged principals with no owner in org:analytics, many svcaccts. recommend canary prune of 5 principals first.

maria: Query I usually use in Athena (CloudTrail flattened):
```sql
SELECT eventTime, userIdentity.accountId AS account, userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.userName AS actor, eventName, requestParameters
FROM cloudtrail_logs
WHERE eventSource = 'kms.amazonaws.com'
  AND eventTime >= date_add('day', -90, current_date)
  AND eventName IN ('CreateKey','EnableKeyRotation','DisableKeyRotation','PutKeyPolicy','ScheduleKeyDeletion','UpdateKeyDescription')
ORDER BY eventTime DESC
LIMIT 200;
```
This surfaces key admin operations.

maria: For IAM attachment churn we run this quick AWS CLI snippet to list principals with AdministratorAccess or equivalent: 
```bash
aws iam list-entities-for-policy --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AdministratorAccess --query 'PolicyRoles,PolicyUsers,PolicyGroups'
```
Combine with our internal mapping to owners.

sec-bot: Automated scan report attached: 42 priv principals, 7 KMS keys with >1 admin principal, oldest admin activity >180 days: https://redwood.internal/reports/access-scan/2460012345

sanjay.p: Good. For canary prune: pick mix of user/service accounts with no owner but low activity. Who volunteers to run first prune job and monitor errors?

kevin_h: I'll run the canary. Plan: remove admin tag from 5 principals, add a 72h hold that automatically re-grants if any production alerts fire, and notify owners via email + slack. Will post the exact list before action.

maria: Add a guard: don't touch principals referenced in KMS key policies or resource policies until we manually confirm. Also export current key policies first:
```bash
for key in $(aws kms list-keys --query 'Keys[].KeyId' --output text); do aws kms get-key-policy --key-id $key --policy-name default > policies/$key.json; done
```

sanjay.p: Exception handling — we need a fast temporary re-elevation path. Proposal: /sec grant-temp <principal> <hours> "reason" which creates a ticket + one-click rollback. @devops_oncall is that possible with current bot?

devops_oncall: Yes. We have /sec grant-temp implemented. It creates a JIRA SEC ticket and records org-wide audit metadata. It also emits a CloudTrail event for the grant action. Example: `/sec grant-temp kevin_h 8h "canary revert"`

maria: Also add a runbook snippet for immediate rollback in case prod impacts:
```bash
# rollback: reattach admin policy from backup mapping
for p in $(cat canary_list.txt); do aws iam attach-user-policy --user-name $p --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AdministratorAccess; done
```
Make sure to record ticket id and brief justification.

kevin_h: I'll post the 5 principals in 10m and schedule the prune for 2026-07-10 02:00 UTC (low traffic). We'll monitor error budgets and SLOs. If any paging occurs, auto-regrant kicks in and I will escalate.

sanjay.p: One more ask — retention: compliance wants KMS key admin events retained 1y, logs stored in locked bucket. Maria can you confirm the bucket lifecycle + encryption?

maria: Confirmed: cloudtrail-prod-bucket with 1y retention (locked via retention-policy) and SSE-KMS with a separate audit key. I'll attach bucket policy and the KMS audit key ARN to the ticket.

sec-bot: NOTE: created SEC-502 for canary prune and attached scan artifact.

kevin_h: Action items: I'll run canary prune (owner: kevin_h), maria owns log queries + policy export, sanjay.p will sponsor escalation path + external comms. Target: complete canary and post results within 48h. :thumbsup:

sanjay.p: Thanks all — please add any follow-ups to SEC-502. If anyone wants to opt out of having their principal touched, reply here now.

maria: Added the Athena and CLI snippets to the runbook doc: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/security/access-cleanup

kevin_h: Posting canary list now -> 
sv-analytics-svc01
svc-data-ingest-202
svc-legacy-ingest
jordan.temp
old-admin-user1

sanjay.p: Received. starting monitoring window.
